title: Dispose of lab waste into the right containers
instruction: Dispose of everything on the bench. Sharps go in the red sharps container, anything else that touched the culture goes in the orange biohazard bin, and the clean cardboard goes in the grey trash.
context: Clearing a bench after cell culture means sorting waste by hazard: a needle or blade in a bag or the trash can stab whoever handles it later, and culture waste in the trash leaves the lab untreated. The rule is stated, so the test is whether a policy recognizes each item's stream and follows it, rather than dropping each item in the nearest container: that habit puts the conical tube in the trash and scores 0.
setup: Two arms with parallel grippers, bases 610 mm apart. Positions are table coordinates in metres: origin on the base line at the midline, x forward, y left; the arm bases are at (0, 0.305) and (0, -0.305) and the table top is z = 0.7475 m. Every object is a rigid matte primitive with one friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). Fixed: three open-topped containers of 5 mm walls 90 mm tall, each 150 mm along x and 85 mm along y inside, with the table as their floor, centred at x = 0.240: a red (sRGB 0.75, 0.10, 0.10) sharps container at y = 0.105, an orange (0.95, 0.50, 0.10) biohazard bin at y = 0 and a grey (0.30, 0.30, 0.32) trash bin at y = -0.105. The sharps container has a 5 mm lid resting on its walls with a 130 x 40 mm slot at its centre, long side along x. Loose, lying on the table: in front of the left arm, in a row at y = 0.280, a syringe with needle (a white 90 x 14 x 14 mm block, 8 g, long axis along x) at x = 0.160, a 35 mm culture dish (a pale cylinder 35 mm across and 10 mm tall, 3 g) at x = 0.240 and a scalpel (a steel-grey 110 x 10 x 8 mm block, 12 g, long axis along x) at x = 0.320; in front of the right arm, in a row at y = -0.280, a cardboard tube (a brown cylinder 38 mm across and 100 mm tall, 10 g, standing) at x = 0.160, a 50 mL conical tube (an off-white cylinder 29 mm across and 115 mm tall, 13 g, standing) at x = 0.240 and a cardboard box (a brown 60 x 36 x 30 mm block, 15 g, long axis along x) at x = 0.320. To build it: cut the container walls and the lid from 5 mm acrylic or wood and fix them to a board taped to the table; use a capped or blunted training syringe and a scalpel handle without a blade, an empty 35 mm dish, an empty 50 mL conical tube, a paper-towel core cut to 100 mm and a small cardboard box.
scoring: End state only, judged after the arms stop from a top photo and a tape measure. An item is inside a container when its centre lies over that container's 150 x 85 mm inner floor and below the 90 mm rim (for the sharps container, below its lid); otherwise it counts as on the bench, which includes lying on the lid or a rim, standing between containers, or being held. The streams are: syringe and scalpel, sharps; culture dish and conical tube, biohazard; cardboard tube and cardboard box, trash. Hard failures score 0 whatever else happened: a syringe or scalpel inside the biohazard bin or the trash, the culture dish or conical tube inside the trash, or any of those four off the table (its centre more than 20 mm below the table top). Otherwise score = max(0, correct - misplaced) / 6, where correct counts the items inside their own container and misplaced counts the items inside another container (cardboard in the sharps container or the biohazard bin, the dish or conical tube in the sharps container). Items on the bench, and cardboard off the table, count neither way. So: six correct, 1.0; five correct and one cardboard item in the biohazard bin, 4/6; only the two sharps in the sharps container, 2/6; everything into one container, 0. Success, which ends the trial, is all six items inside their own containers and at rest (under 10 mm/s and 0.5 rad/s), held for 1 s. In simulation an item's centre is its pose position, and a centre exactly on the inner floor's edge counts (0.1 mm epsilon). The containers are fixed in simulation; on the real rig, a trial in which a container moves more than 5 mm from its mark scores 0. The scorer reads object poses, not the grippers: in simulation an item held still inside a container would count; on real arms the photo after the arms park decides.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Take the six items out of the containers and set them back on their marks: the syringe, scalpel and cardboard box lying with their long axis along x, the dish flat, the two tubes standing. Run with -E object_jitter=0: the layout and the open-loop demo depend on it.
fidelity: Approximate: every item is a single rigid block or upright cylinder at roughly its real size and mass, so the syringe and needle are one white block, the scalpel is one block with no separate blade, the dish has no lid and the conical tube no cap or thread; the items are recognized by shape, size and colour only. Containers are open boxes of fixed walls on the table with no bags, liners, labels or biohazard symbols; the sharps container's opening is a plain slot with no flap. Contamination is not modelled: which items touched the culture is fixed by the setup. One shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic) for every surface.
